protocol.research_question: In adults undergoing primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty, does tranexamic acid administered intravenously, topically, or by combined routes reduce perioperative total blood loss compared with placebo or no tranexamic acid, and what is its effect on allogeneic transfusion rate and symptomatic venous thromboembolic events?

pico.population: Adults undergoing primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty.
pico.intervention: Tranexamic acid administered intravenously, topically (intra-articular), or by combined routes.
pico.outcome_primary: Total blood loss, measured in millilitres (mL).
outcomes_secondary: Allogeneic blood transfusion rate (dichotomous; proportion of patients receiving allogeneic blood transfusion).
Symptomatic venous thromboembolic events (dichotomous; deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism within 30 days).

inclusion_criteria: Adults undergoing primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty.
Intervention: tranexamic acid administered intravenously, topically (intra-articular), or by combined routes.
Comparator: placebo or no tranexamic acid.
Reports at least one of the following outcomes: total blood loss (mL), allogeneic blood transfusion rate, or symptomatic venous thromboembolic events within 30 days.
exclusion_criteria: Bilateral or simultaneous bilateral knee arthroplasty.
Studies not evaluating tranexamic acid in the specified population or with an ineligible comparator.
Duplicate publications or overlapping patient populations, with only the most informative report included.
Studies without extractable data for the primary or secondary outcomes.
subgroup_variables: Route of tranexamic acid administration (intravenous vs topical vs combined)
interventions: Tranexamic acid administered by combined routes

characteristics.title: Topical Tranexamic Acid Reduces Blood Loss in Minimally Invasive Total Knee Arthroplasty Receiving Rivaroxaban.
characteristics.study_design: Prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled trial (parallel, three-arm) - source wording: 'This prospective, randomized, controlled trial demonstrated...' and 'Our prospective, randomized, double-blind trial'
characteristics.population_description: Patients aged 40 years or more who underwent unilateral primary minimally invasive total knee arthroplasty; 93 patients enrolled (23 male and 70 female). Exclusion criteria included documented history of thromboembolic disease, cardiovascular disease (myocardial infarction or angina), stroke, coagulopathy, lifelong warfarin treatment, impaired hepatic or renal function, allergy to TXA, and preoperative anemia (Hb <= 10 g/dL). All patients received oral rivaroxaban 10 mg daily for thromboprophylaxis.
characteristics.intervention_description: Tranexamic acid by two routes. Intravenous (IV) group (n = 31) received 1 g TXA (20 mL) intravenously 10 minutes before skin closure. Topical group (n = 32) received 3 g (60 mL) TXA (Transamin 50 mg/mL) in 100 mL saline intra-articularly via the drain after capsule closure (final volume 160 mL). Drainage tubes clamped for 1 hour after injection.
characteristics.control_description: Placebo group (n = 30) received saline twice: 20 mL intravenously 10 minutes before skin closure and 160 mL intra-articularly via the drain after capsule closure before deflation of the tourniquet. No tranexamic acid administered.
characteristics.follow_up_duration: Postoperative clinic follow-up at 2, 6, and 12 weeks (clinical follow-up for 3 months).

outcome.rationale: Table 2 reports 'Total blood loss (mL)', the review's prespecified primary continuous outcome, in millilitres.

population.rationale: Participants were adults aged 40 years or more undergoing unilateral primary minimally invasive TKA, which falls within the protocol's primary unilateral TKA population.
population.quote: Between August 2015 and April 2016, a consecutive series of 145 patients aged 40 years or more who underwent unilateral primary minimally invasive TKA were assessed in terms of their eligibility for inclusion in this study.

contrast.rationale: Randomized comparison of intravenous tranexamic acid (1 g IV) versus placebo (saline both intravenously and intra-articularly), matching the review's intervention and comparator.

components.source_component:
The primary outcome measured was the estimated total blood loss. Hemoglobin (Hb) and hematocrit (Hct) levels were measured on PODs 1, 2, and 4. The blood volume was assumed to have normalized on the fourth postoperative day. Total blood loss was calculated according to the method of Nadler et al. [ 29 ] using the maximum postoperative decrease in Hb level adjusted for the weight and height of the patient. The formula can be summarized as 
(1) T o t a l b l o o d l o s s = T o t a l b l o o d v o l u m e × m a x i m u m r e d u c t i o n i n H b l e v e l m e a n H b l e v e l + v o l u m e t r a n s f u s e d . 
The secondary outcomes were the rate of perioperative blood transfusion, the rate of deep-vein thrombosis (DVT), wound complications, visual analogue scale (VAS) on POD 1, the length of hospital stay, and the range of motion of the knee. The trigger for allogenic transfusion of red blood cells was set at a Hb level of 8 g/dl in healthy patients, or between 8 and 9 g/dl in patients with clinical symptoms and signs of acute anemia. In patients with cardiovascular disease, the transfusion threshold was set at a Hb level of 9 g/dl. The amount and rate of blood transfusion and the length of hospital stay were recorded in all patients. 

The patients were followed-up at the clinic postoperatively after 2, 6, and 12 weeks. All postoperative conditions, including wound erythema, hematoma, infection, bleedings, and blisters, were recorded. We inspected the appearance of the operated knee, and if the swelling was noted, the knee circumference was measured 1 cm proximal to the upper pole of the patella. If the circumference of operated knee increased ≧3 cm compared with the opposite knee, it was defined as intraarticular hematoma formation. All wound complications requiring return to surgery because of hematoma and infection within 30 days of procedure were recorded. The presence of DVT was detected upon measurement of thigh or leg edema of >3 cm as compared with the contralateral leg in association with calf tenderness or tightness [ 30 ]. Ascending venography of the leg was performed using the Rabinov and Paulin technique [ 31 ] if symptomatic DVT appeared. Computerized tomography of the chest was performed if there was a suspicion of pulmonary embolism. All radiographic images were interpreted by an independent radiologist. 

3. Statistical Analysis 

One-way ANOVA was used to determine differences between the three groups in the demographic characteristics, preoperative clinical data, total blood loss, postoperative drainage amount, postoperative hemoglobin level, length of hospital stay, VAS, range of motion of knee, and wound length. If the one-way ANOVA result was significant ( p < 0.05), post hoc tests were performed to confirm where the differences occurred between the groups. 

Differences in descriptive data, including gender, ASA level, incidence of DVT, blood transfusion rate, and safety outcome, between the three groups were compared using the chi-square test or Fisher's exact test. An intention-to-treat analysis was used in patients who undergone planned surgery, had taken study medications, and withdrew blood for preoperative and postoperative Hb levels. All statistical comparisons were made using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) (version 18; SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA). 

4. Results 

The postoperative results are shown in Table 2 . The wound length under full extension of the knee did not differ between the 3 groups. The Hb levels on POD1, POD2, and POD4 were significantly higher in the topical group than in the placebo group ( p = 0.005, p < 0.001, and p < 0.001, resp.). There were no significant differences in Hb level between the placebo group and the IV group on POD1 and POD2, but the Hb level on POD4 was higher in the IV group than in the placebo group ( p = 0.043). The postoperative drainage amount within 16 hours was higher in the placebo group (409 ± 134 mL) than in the topical group (222 ± 85 mL, p < 0.001) and the IV group (304 ± 147 mL, p = 0.006). The total drainage amount was also higher in the placebo group than in the topical and IV groups (626 ± 149 mL versus 412 ± 122 mL versus 525 ± 185 mL, p < 0.001 and p = 0.041, resp.).

29410968.quality_notes: Study: single-center prospective randomized double-blind trial (NCT02453802); 93 patients undergoing primary unilateral minimally invasive TKA, randomized to 3 parallel arms: placebo (n=30; saline IV + saline intra-articular), IV TXA (n=31; 1 g TXA IV + saline intra-articular), topical TXA (n=32; 3 g TXA in 100 mL saline intra-articular + saline IV). All received oral rivaroxaban 10 mg daily x14 days for thromboprophylaxis. comparative_design set to multi_arm_rct because the source is a 3-arm parallel randomized trial analyzed with pairwise (post hoc) comparisons. Treatment vs control comparisons extracted for the review's route-based subgroup analysis: IV vs placebo and topical vs placebo; the head-to-head topical vs IV comparison (total blood loss p=0.179/0.197) is not a review comparator and was not extracted. Total blood loss is reported as mean (SD; range) in Table 2 (Placebo 1131 [336; 567-1845]; IV 921 [252; 465-1495]; Topical 795 [231; 336-1350]); ranges not entered into min/max fields since mean/SD were reported. Blood transfusion rows use the overall 3-group p=0.102, not a pairwise test. The secondary VTE endpoint was reported by the source as separate components (symptomatic DVT and pulmonary embolism, follow-up up to 3 months) rather than a combined composite; components were kept as reported. One symptomatic DVT occurred in the IV group (1/31); no pulmonary embolism occurred in any arm. Note an internal denominator inconsistency in Table 3: the topical arm is shown as n=31 for the PE and DVT rows but n=32 in Table 1, Table 2 and the text; values were retained exactly as printed in Table 3.

characteristics.title: Efficacy of Different Doses of Intra‐Articular Tranexamic Acid for Reducing Blood Loss and Lower Limb Swelling After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective, Randomized, Controlled Trial
characteristics.study_design: Prospective, randomized, controlled trial (single-center RCT with three parallel arms: two TXA dose arms vs. placebo)
characteristics.population_description: Adults (18 to 80 years of age, ASA I-III) with osteoarthritis of the knee who underwent primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty; recruited from September 2020 to January 2021. Mean age ~65-66 years; predominantly female (e.g., 55/75, 58/75, 51/75 across groups).
characteristics.intervention_description: Intra-articular (topical) tranexamic acid injected into the joint after prosthesis implantation and joint capsule closure: low-dose group B = 20 mL (1 g) TXA; high-dose group C = 60 mL (3 g) TXA. Route: intra-articular/topical only.
characteristics.control_description: Group A received 20 mL of placebo (saline solution) injected into the joint cavity.
characteristics.funding: 1.3.5 Project for Disciplines of Excellence–Clinical Research Incubation Project, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, grant no. ZYJC18040

39673144.quality_notes: Design: single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial with three parallel arms (Group A placebo/saline n=75; Group B intra-articular TXA 1 g n=75; Group C intra-articular TXA 3 g n=75). 225 patients randomized; no loss to follow-up (2-week follow-up). All TXA was administered intra-articular (topical) — no intravenous or combined-route arm, so the prespecified route subgroup is represented only by the topical route. Two TXA dose levels (1 g and 3 g) were compared against the same saline placebo; because a single placebo arm is shared by both dose contrasts, each contrast is reported as a separate row from the multi-arm RCT. Total blood loss (TBL) was not shown numerically in Table 2 (reported in Figure 2 and Results text); values were taken from Results 3.2. A minor discrepancy exists between the abstract (3 g TXA TBL 568.70 ± 408.27 mL) and the Results text (567.7 ± 408.3 mL) — noted as a conflict. Reported between-group p-values for the dichotomous outcomes (transfusion, DVT, CMVT) are overall three-group comparisons (Pearson chi-square), not pairwise; noted. Time horizon: the trial followed patients 2 weeks (DVT assessed by Doppler ultrasound on postoperative day 14); the protocol's VTE secondary outcome specifies within 30 days, and this paper's follow-up is shorter. HSS score, range of motion, VAS pain, lower-limb swelling, hemoglobin decrease, IBL, HBL, length of stay, and wound complications were reported but are not among the protocol's requested outcomes and were not extracted.
